a disease, such as measles, which has a threshold density of population, and which is not affected by deaths from other causes, and which is the only cause, or nearly the only cause, of death, will, when introduced into a population of a density below the threshold, die out; and, if the population is above the threshold, it will become endemic, and will reach a state of steady prevalence.

if the threshold density of population is exceeded, the disease will be endemic and will tend towards a steady state of a particular nature, depending on the nature of the functions characterizing infectivity, morbility, etc. If the threshold density of the population is not exceeded the disease will die out.
